summary: Discovery for open-model selection and deployment mode. Borealis needs multilingual support (EN/ES/PT), long context (up to 64k for doc summarization), and tool-calling for retrieval/DB lookups. Team is evaluating Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) with security constraints (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Next steps: pricing, security pack, pilot plan, technical deep-dive.

latency vs cost and quantization options
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-12-10 15:00 PST
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (AE, Redwood); Miguel Santos (SE, Redwood); Anika Rao (CTO, Borealis Data); Tom Braddock (Head ML); Lydia Chen (PM); Marcus Yeo (Infra)

[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Jenna with Redwood, this is Miguel from our solutions team. Quick round robin, say who you are.
[00:06] Anika Rao: Hi I'm Anika, CTO at Borealis. We're evaluating inference for our AI doc product.
[00:09] Tom Braddock: Tom here, lead on the ML side.
[00:11] Lydia Chen: Lydia, PM, I'll own the pilot coordination.
[00:14] Miguel Santos: Great. Quick agenda: model selection (open models), context length needs, multilingual, tool calling, and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private).

[00:30] Jenna: Anika, can you give a bit of background on what you're trying to build and the most important success criteria?
[00:36] Anika: Sure. We do long-form document summarization and Q&A for enterprise customers, legal/fintech mostly. Need to support English, Spanish, Portuguese. Typical user session is a 20–50 page doc bundle, so context needs are big—some cases we want full 64k, most are 32k. Also need tool calling for retrieval + vector DB lookups, and we need deterministic behavior for some flows. Cost matters but reliability more so, for enterprise SLAs.

[01:15] Miguel: Understood. On models, are you looking at closed models or open-source variants? Any preference for quantized weights for cost?
[01:22] Tom: We're leaning open models to avoid API lock-in and for cost control. Quality must be close to SOTA, especially for multilingual. We have some latency constraints—95th percentile under 1s for short queries, for long summaries we can accept higher.

[02:05] Jenna: For open-models, people commonly compare Llama/Open models, Mistral, and some of the 100b open weights. Redwood's catalog includes verified performance profiles for several. Miguel, want to talk variants?

[02:15] Miguel: Yeah. So typical tradeoffs: larger models give better accuracy on summarization and multilingual nuance, but they cost more and increase latency. With Redwood Hosted we expose multiple model variants and automatic fallbacks—if a model is out of capacity you can route to a cheaper variant. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for consistent latency. Private/VPC gives you control over networking, KMS, and on-prem for compliance. There are also quantized variants that can run at lower cost but might slightly drop quality, especially for non-English languages.

[03:00] Tom: Quick question — how do you handle 64k context? We have some legal customers that want full-case ingest.

[03:08] Miguel: Two approaches. One is models compiled with extended context support (32k/64k) and kernel selection tuned. Another is Redwood's prefix/KV cache and chunking + rerank pipeline. For true 64k you generally want model that supports it natively or use efficient attention kernels. On Dedicated we can provision infra optimized for longer contexts to keep latency reasonable. Note: sometimes the transcription/notes incorrectly call it "KV cash" in our older docs — sorry for the typo.

[03:50] Anika: And multilingual — do quantized models degrade more for Spanish/Portuguese?

[03:55] Miguel: Yes, quantization tends to affect low-resource languages more. Our optimize toolkit recommends quantization profiles per workload; for multilingual workloads we often keep FP16 or int8 with careful calibration, and we run quick evals. We'll propose model+quantization combos in the pilot.

[04:30] Lydia: Tool-calling — we need the model to call our retrieval API and a DB lookup. How robust is function calling across open models?

[04:36] Miguel: Good question. Function/tool calling is mature on several of the model families but not all open checkpoints expose the same interface. On Redwood we provide a normalized tool-calling layer: you define schema for tool inputs/outputs and Redwood routes the call and returns structured results. Some models are better at deterministic JSON output; others need post-processing. We'll recommend models that have strong structured output behavior.

[05:20] Tom: For hosted vs dedicated — our execs prefer hosted for faster iteration, but infra wants private for data residency and KMS. If we start hosted, can we migrate to private later without redoing prompts?

[05:30] Jenna: That's exactly where Redwood shines — we aim for consistent API and rollout semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private. You should be able to pin model versions and migrate with minimal prompt changes. We do advise capturing prompt engineering and temp seeds, but most customers transition smoothly.

[06:05] Marcus Yeo: On the VPC side, what's the network pattern? We have strict firewalls and need to use our KMS and SAML SSO.

[06:12] Miguel: For Private we can do customer-managed VPC peering or private link equivalents, and integrate with your KMS (we support common KMS/HSM integrations). SSO/SAML and RBAC are standard. We'll bring infra docs in the next email. Expect some set up work on firewalls and routing.

[06:50] Anika: What about observability — we need per-request latency and token-level cost breakdowns to bill back clients.

[06:56] Jenna: Redwood Console shows per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost/latency, tracing hooks. For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and export logs to your SIEM.

[07:25] Tom: Competitors — any gotchas vs Anthropic or OpenAI?

[07:28] Miguel: I won't call out everything but common differences: Anthropic has strong safety and family-of-models consistency; OpenAI has scale and deep tool-chain integrations. With Redwood you get control over model variants, deployment modes, and unit economics — so for infra-heavy or compliance-heavy customers we often land on Dedicated or Private.

[08:05] Lydia: Pricing ballpark?

[08:08] Jenna: I'll send hosted per-token rates and example cost breakdowns. Dedicated is commit-based monthly with predictable throughput; Private has a platform fee plus infra. We'll include examples in the docs.

[08:30] Anika: For pilot, what would you recommend we run to validate multilingual quality and 64k context?

[08:36] Miguel: Two-track pilot: 1) Run a set of benchmark prompts in EN/ES/PT across a few model families (32k vs 64k variants) with your prompt suite. 2) End-to-end integration test for tool-calling and retrieval latencies with a small dedicated pool or hosted with reserved capacity. We'll measure accuracy (f1/rouge or custom metrics), latency P50/P95, and cost.

[09:10] Tom: How long for the eval? We prefer short — like 2 weeks.

[09:13] Jenna: Two weeks is doable. We'll draft a benchmark spreadsheet and run the tests—Miguel will own setup.

[09:30] Anika: Security — can you confirm Redwood's compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO)? We need support for audit logs and data residency controls.

[09:36] Jenna: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, ISO for enterprise. We support audit logs, SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For data residency we can discuss Private deployments or region-pinning on Hosted. We'll attach the security pack.

[10:05] Marcus: Tokenization differences across languages — any pitfalls?

[10:11] Miguel: Tokenizers vary between families; we often recommend tokenization-aware cost estimates. For Spanish/Portuguese token counts are usually reasonable, but for some languages morphological differences matter. We'll include tokenization samples and per-language token costs.

[10:45] Lydia: If we go Dedicated, how fast can we provision GPU pools?

[10:50] Jenna: Depends on inventory; typical lead time is weeks to a couple months for large committed pools, but we offer burst and temporary reserved capacity to bridge. For pilots we can often get a small pool online in under two weeks.

[11:20] Tom: Any recommended models for multilingual summarization with good function-calling?

[11:26] Miguel: From our catalog: a tuned Mistral-family 70b-ish variant does well for EN/ES/PT at 32k. For 64k we suggest a native 64k-attention model — some 100b open checkpoints or specialized long-context variants. We'll list exact IDs in the follow-up. Also consider an ensemble: smaller faster model for short queries, larger one for long summarizations.

[12:00] Anika: We also need deterministic outputs for compliance flows — is that feasible?

[12:07] Miguel: You can increase determinism via sampling temperature=0, beam/greedy decoding, and controlling model seeds. For production, Redwood supports pinning model versions and deterministic configs; some randomness still exists in certain model families, we'll highlight tradeoffs.

[12:40] Jenna: Recap / next steps: Jenna sends pricing + security docs; Miguel to prepare benchmark plan and prompt sets for EN/ES/PT and 32k/64k; Tom to share telemetry and latency targets; Lydia to confirm stakeholders and timeline. We'll aim to start the 2-week pilot the week of 12/20 if all good.

[13:05] Anika: Sounds good. One last Q — can Redwood run a small live benchmark on our data without sending full PII off to hosted?

[13:12] Miguel: Yes — options: we can run benchmarks inside your VPC with Private, or redact/sanitize data for hosted evals, or do a short on-prem run. We'll include options.

[13:30] Jenna: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive.

[13:35] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcription had a few small errors (product names and acronyms). Shared artifacts referenced: /docs/redwood/security-pack.pdf (link), /benchmarks/borealis-prompt-set.xlsx (to be shared), pricing example spreadsheet (sent post-call).
